items.title: What is the pin index position for an oxygen cylinder?
items.explanation: Oxygen uses pins 2 and 5. Nitrous oxide uses 3 and 5, medical air 1 and 5, and Entonox a single pin at 7. The pin index stops the wrong cylinder being fitted.

items.title: Which neuromuscular blocker is depolarising?
items.explanation: Succinylcholine is the only depolarising muscle relaxant in routine use. The others are non-depolarising.

items.title: What is the normal end-tidal CO2 (EtCO2) range in a healthy adult?
items.explanation: Normal EtCO2 is about 35–45 mmHg. Capnography is also the best quick confirmation that the tube is in the trachea.

items.title: Cricoid pressure is also known as:
items.options:
Sellick's manoeuvre
Jaw thrust
BURP manoeuvre
Trendelenburg position
items.explanation: Cricoid pressure (Sellick's manoeuvre) presses the cricoid cartilage backwards to help reduce the risk of regurgitation during rapid sequence induction.

items.title: A standard steam autoclave cycle for wrapped instruments is:
items.options:
100 °C for 5 minutes
121 °C for 15 minutes
60 °C for 30 minutes
160 °C for 10 minutes
items.explanation: A common steam sterilisation cycle is 121 °C at about 15 psi for 15 minutes (or 134 °C for about 3 minutes). Hot-air ovens use much higher temperatures for longer.

items.title: In the ASA physical status classification, ASA III means:
items.options:
A normal healthy patient
Mild systemic disease
Severe systemic disease
A brain-dead organ donor
items.explanation: ASA I is healthy, ASA II mild systemic disease, ASA III severe systemic disease, ASA IV severe disease that is a constant threat to life, ASA V moribund and ASA VI a brain-dead organ donor.

items.title: The Mallampati classification helps to:
items.options:
Grade post-operative pain
Predict a difficult airway
Measure depth of anaesthesia
Assess the risk of bleeding
items.explanation: Mallampati grades how much of the oropharynx is visible with the mouth open and tongue out. Higher classes suggest intubation may be more difficult.

items.title: MAC (minimum alveolar concentration) of an inhalational agent is the concentration that:
items.options:
Causes apnoea in 50% of patients
Prevents movement to a surgical incision in 50% of patients
Prevents awareness in 100% of patients
Causes loss of consciousness in 95% of patients
items.explanation: MAC is the alveolar concentration at 1 atmosphere that prevents movement in response to a surgical skin incision in 50% of patients. It is used to compare the potency of inhalational agents.
